It highlights a roadmap for 60 GW renewable capacity by 2032, an Energy Compact at the UN, and efforts beyond generation to build a clean energy ecosystem. NTPC is pioneering India's first hydrogen hub, green hydrogen pilots for hard-to-abate sectors, and an integrated technology approach combining renewables with battery storage, digital operations, and electric/hydrogen mobility for a resilient, just transition.

nodes.title: Stakeholder Engagement and Materiality Assessment
nodes.summary: NTPC emphasizes stakeholder engagement and materiality assessment to create value. It engages diverse stakeholders (employees, communities, contractors, customers, vendors, government, regulators, investors, media, citizens) through various modes and frequencies, using a 4-step stakeholder management process. Key concerns and materiality topics are linked to each stakeholder group. The materiality assessment follows a structured 5-phase methodology, conducted every 3-4 years with internal and external stakeholders, to prioritize material topics, which inform decision-making, risk management, and strategic planning for long-term sustainability. The approach aligns with IIRC Framework and GRI standards, with details available on NTPC's website.

Topics include occupational health and safety (SAP safety framework, zero-incident target, safety academy), business ethics (code of conduct, whistle-blower policy), energy management (efficiency groups, EEMS), climate change (RE capacity target, decommissioning old plants), digital transformation (digital platforms, CPM & BI tools), water management (CEO Water Mandate, ZLD, air-cooled condensers), labour practices (human rights policy, bipartite council, CLIMS), air emissions (FGD/DSI, CEMS), community engagement (CSR policy, NTPC Foundation), governance practices (board committees, audits), economic value creation (direct economic value), waste management (approved disposal, e-auction), supply chain management (sustainable policy, ESG data), new businesses (renewables, green hydrogen), employee development (HR re-engineering, job rotation), biodiversity (policy, 40M saplings, wildlife projects), and innovation & R&D (NETRA, patented tech, CCU).

nodes.title: Financial Capital
nodes.summary: The text covers NTPC's financial capital management, emphasizing CAPEX for long-term objectives, digitalization for operational efficiency, and high capital productivity. It details financial highlights for FY 2024-25, including consolidated revenue of ₹1,90,862.45 crore, PAT of ₹23,953 crore, and economic value retained of ₹30,576.19 crore. It discusses corporate governance, asset utilization, cost optimization, and revenue growth from non-fossil ventures. Financial achievements include a net profit of ₹23,953.15 crore (consolidated) and ₹19,649.41 crore (standalone), over 100% realization of billed amounts, a weighted average borrowing cost of 6.61%, and highest credit ratings. The strategic approach balances energy security and transition, with segment-wise CAPEX of ₹44,635.62 crore allocated to coal, renewables, hydro, storage, and digital initiatives. CSR spending was ₹363 crore, exceeding the 2% limit, alongside environmental sustainability initiatives. Economic value generated was ₹1,90,243.38 crore, distributed across operating costs, wages, capital providers, government, and community investments. The text also covers government financial assistance (none received), climate considerations in financial planning, and revenue diversification with ₹17,359.67 crore (9.3% of total) from non-fossil sources.

nodes.title: NTPC Asset Management and Power Generation Overview
nodes.summary: The page covers NTPC's asset management approach, focusing on optimal performance, reliability, and longevity through risk-based maintenance, real-time monitoring, and audits. It also details power generation: NTPC operates 103 power stations, generated 438 BU in FY 2024-25 (3.9% growth), and achieved 45.66% growth in non-fossil capacity. Installed capacity is 78.61 GW (including 19.78 GW from allied companies), representing ~17% of India's capacity and ~25% of supply. A table shows gross capacity and generation from FY 2022-23 to FY 2024-25 for coal, gas/liquid, hydro, and renewable energy, totaling 78,610 MW and 438.66 BU in FY 2024-25.

nodes.title: Strategic Fuel Management
nodes.summary: NTPC's strategic fuel management emphasizes sustainable production, operational efficiency, and responsible resource use to minimize primary resources like coal, gas, biomass, and water. It details coal sourcing through long-term FSAs with CIL and SCCL, captive mines, MoU-based arrangements, open market procurement, and reduced imported coal. Gas sourcing covers long-term GSAs, RLNG contracts, spot procurement, and IGX diversification, noting nil domestic gas supply since 2021. Biomass sourcing highlights NTPC as India's first utility to commercialize biomass co-firing up to 10%, with contracts for biomass pellets, procurement strategy, and benefits like carbon reduction and rural employment.

nodes.title: NTPC Fuel Sourcing: Coal, Gas, and Biomass Diversification
nodes.summary: NTPC optimizes resource use to reduce tariffs and protect ecosystems, diversifying fuel for energy security. Coal sourcing covers long-term FSAs with CIL and SCCL (196.37 MMT and 27.99 MMT ACQ), 90% materialization, captive mines (41.1 MMT), NLCIL and THDCIL MoUs (6.09 and 3.49 MMT), open market procurement (2.91 MMT), and imported coal (1.755 MMT). Gas sourcing includes GAIL GSAs until 2026, nil domestic gas since 2021 due to CGD priority, 1.36 MMSCMD RLNG contract until 2028, spot RLNG via tenders and single offer, commitment-based spot RLNG, liquid fuel reserves, IGX procurement since 2023, and FY 2024-25 consumption of 913 MMSCM plus 86 MMSCM diverted to RGPPL. Biomass sourcing highlights first commercial co-firing up to 10%, carbon reduction, rural income, UNFCCC recognition, scaled contracts for 7.48 MMT pellets across 23 stations, 979,143 MT received, and Biofuel Circle procurement for Mouda.

It details tenders for Dadri and APCPL Jhajjar, and expansion to Eastern, Southern, and North-Eastern regions. Biomass co-firing benefits are highlighted. The renewable energy section outlines NTPC's 60 GW target by 2032, subsidiaries (NGEL, NREL, THDC, NEEPCO), and a diverse portfolio: solar, wind, small hydro, floating solar, UMREPPs, energy storage, and green hydrogen. It includes a project snapshot table, land bank with ISTS connectivity for 6.1 GW, outsourcing model (5 GW commissioned, 3 GW execution, 9.5 GW tendering), UMREPPs (6 GW), floating solar (262 MW operating, 316 MW execution, 1 GW pipeline), and energy storage solutions (pumped hydro, BESS, hydrogen) with examples at Khavda and Chushul.

nodes.title: Renewable Energy
nodes.summary: NTPC's biomass co-firing initiatives include a tender for Dadri with 279 bidders and awards expected by April 2025, and 1,060 TPD biomass awarded to 47 vendors for Jhajjar. NTPC is expanding procurement to Eastern, Southern, and North-Eastern regions. The program reduces coal dependence, promotes sustainable agriculture, and addresses stubble burning, aligning with ESG goals. NTPC targets 60 GW renewable capacity by 2032 through subsidiaries NGEL, NREL, THDC, and NEEPCO, developing solar, wind, hybrid, FDRE, storage, and green hydrogen projects. As of March 31, 2025, 6.8 GW renewable capacity is commissioned (6.2 GW solar, 0.6 GW wind, 0.03 GW small hydro). The text also includes a detailed project portfolio snapshot with counts by status (commissioned, execution, tendering) and technology, and a land bank overview.

nodes.title: Renewable Energy Expansion and Storage Solutions
nodes.summary: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited has developed a strategic land bank with ISTS connectivity for 6.1 GW of upcoming projects, including 3.7 GW solar in Rajasthan, 2.1 GW in Andhra Pradesh, and 0.3 GW in Madhya Pradesh. NTPC has commissioned over 5 GW of solar through an outsourcing model, with 3 GW under execution and 9.5 GW under tendering. It is developing Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power Parks (UMREPPs) totaling 6 GW, including 4.8 GW in Gujarat, 0.7 GW under DVC, and 0.6 GW in Madhya Pradesh. NTPC operates 262 MW of floating solar across five locations, with 316 MW under execution and 1 GW in pipeline. For energy storage, NTPC is developing pumped storage hydro, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and hydrogen-based storage. Notable projects include a 500 kW solar off-grid system with 250 kW/1200 kWh BESS at Khavda and a 200 kW round-the-clock hydrogen project at Chushul. NTPC has tendered 6.4 GW/31.9 GWh of storage and is constructing a 500 MW/3000 MWh system. As one of four Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies, NTPC met its 15 GW tendering target. MoUs include NTPC-GRIDCO & CRUT for green hydrogen mobility in Odisha, NTPC-GAIL for clean energy technologies, NGEL-Bihar for `10,000 Crore renewable projects, and NGEL-Madhya Pradesh for up to 20 GW. Small-scale projects: NVVN handles rooftop solar for 16 central ministries and MHA divisions via RESCO and PMC modes, with pan-India empanelment. NVVN awarded over 66 MW in NTPC townships, commissioned 3.979 MW, 185 MW under construction. NVVN has a work order for 3.45 MW rooftop solar in Andaman & Nicobar under PMC, and facilitates rooftop solar in eight states under PM Surya Ghar. NVVN is the BESS Implementing Agency under VGF scheme: Market Component tender for 500 MW/1000 MWh standalone BESS with LoAs issued and BESPAs signed; CPSU Component tenders for 250 MW/1000 MWh in Uttar Pradesh (with greenhouse option) and 500 MW/1000 MWh in Rajasthan, both pending bid opening.

As of March 31, 2025, 733 MW was commissioned; in FY 2024-25, 5,504 MUs of bundled solar power (including 939 MUs standalone) was supplied to DISCOMs across 12 states and DVC, enhancing energy security and sustainability. nodes.title: FUEL RELATED REFORMS
nodes.summary: The text outlines two fuel-related reforms. Second, it covers the revised biomass policy under TPP Rules, 2023, mandating thermal power stations to co-fire 5% biomass pellets from FY 2024-25 and 7% from FY 2025-26, with MOP announcing benchmark prices for NCR, WR, and NR regions in August and November 2023.

nodes.title: RENEWABLE ENERGY RELATED REFORMS

It also discusses opportunities from rising power demand driven by technology, manufacturing, EVs, and cooling, along with India's 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030. nodes.summary: The page details revenue recognition for energy trading, consultancy, and various government schemes (DDUGJY, SAUBHAGYA, RDSS), specifying timing (over time or point in time), variable consideration, billing, and payment terms. nodes.title: VI. Practical expedients applied as per Ind AS 115:
nodes.summary: The section covers Ind AS 115 practical expedients: no disclosure of remaining performance obligations for short-term contracts or completed performance, no time value adjustment for contracts ≤1 year, and no incremental contract acquisition costs. nodes.title: VI. Practical expedients applied as per Ind AS 115: (intro)

nodes.title: Lease Accounting, Impairment, Segments, Business Combinations, and Dividends

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Recognition, Measurement, Classification, and De-recognition
key_items: Debt instrument at FVTOCI (Fair value through OCI)
Debt instrument at FVTPL (Fair value through profit or loss)

nodes.title: Impairment of financial assets

It then addresses financial liabilities, including initial recognition, classification, subsequent measurement at amortized cost or fair value through profit or loss, and derecognition. It also covers interest rate benchmark reform, financial guarantee contracts, derivative financial instruments, offsetting of financial assets and liabilities, and non-current assets held for sale.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities, Impairment, Derivatives, and Offsetting Policies
key_items: Financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss

22.6 Offsetting of financial assets and financial liabilities
nodes.summary: The page covers impairment recognition for financial assets, distinguishing between 12-month and lifetime ECL based on credit risk changes, and loss allowances for purchased credit-impaired assets.
